correctness.rationale: Independent score calculation for the two Poisson means gives determinant e0 e1 g²/f: the downstream-only rank-one contribution cancels in the determinant and the source measurement supplies the second direction. With d=μ−λ, r=λ/d and t=exp(−dx), logarithmic differentiation gives the stated quadratic P. Its roots have negative product, P(0)>0 and P(1)=−2, giving a simple unique root in (0,1), with strict unimodality and the asserted distance cap. At the root the t derivative of the log-score is negative, while its p derivative is 1/[p+(1−p)t]², giving dx*/dp<0. Writing P=rp+b t−a t², the positive root (b+sqrt(b²+4arp))/(2a) yields t*/p→r/(1−r) for r<1 after rationalization, t*/sqrt(p)→1/sqrt(2) at r=1, and t*→(r−1)/(r+1) for r>1. This gives every displayed distance limit, including constants. The opening 'half the logarithmic slope' means half the limiting supercritical coefficient as μ decreases to 2λ, not half the coefficient at an arbitrary fixed μ>2λ; the exact formulas are unambiguous. This is a local design at a nominal p with known rates and fixed efforts, not a uniform finite-sample guarantee.
